findings.title: Authorization check for team admin uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` requires the user to be both admin and owner, which is wrong. Legitimate team admins who are not owners are denied. Separately, `isAttendee` lets any attendee, matched only by email, add arbitrary guests to someone else's booking. Authorization is also unchecked against booking status, so cancelled or past bookings can be modified.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and the input is not deduplicated
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased, but the guest email is compared without lowercasing, so `Foo@x.com` bypasses the blacklist. Comparison against existing attendees is also case-sensitive. Duplicates within `guests` are not removed server-side, because the uniqueness check exists only in the client. Direct API calls can create duplicate attendees.

findings.title: Calendar update failure is unhandled after the DB write, and the guest list is sent unfiltered to emails
findings.body: The attendees are already persisted when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs. If it throws, the mutation fails with the DB already changed and no emails are sent, so retrying yields a 'must be unique' error. Also, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Guests who were already attendees therefore get the 'scheduled' email again. Errors in the catch block are swallowed with only a console.log.

findings.title: EventManager built from the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's
findings.body: Credentials and user come from `ctx.user`, but the calendar events belong to the booking organizer. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the update targets the wrong credentials and the organizer's calendar event is not updated.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore the disable-standard-emails metadata and send to all attendees
findings.body: Unlike the sibling senders, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not honor `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. New guests also receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, which sends the email to the whole attendee list.

findings.title: Error toast message is built unconditionally, so the fallback never applies
findings.body: The template string is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code. The toast shows 'CODE: message', for example 'BAD_REQUEST: ...'. The `isInvalidEmail` error is also never cleared once the input is corrected.

findings.title: Subject uses attendees[0] name
findings.body: The subject uses `attendees[0].name`, which is correct for the original booker. The newly added guests have an empty name, so the guest-add emails lose useful context. The `name` default of "" may also render badly in the `to:` address as ` <email>`.
